messages:
anya (oncall): heads-up — we started seeing token-stream tail latency spikes from southlake-gpu-pool at ~08:12 UTC. grpc streaming shows a big uptick in out-of-order packets and duplicate acks. metric snapshot: streaming_p95_tokens=320ms -> 2.1s, rpc_retries=+34%

sre-bot: Alert INC-2026-489 created for southlake-gpu-pool:streaming-degradation :rotating_light:

nina (infra): did we push any switch/fw changes overnight in SFL?

raj (runtime): kube-proxy/conntrack roll started 07:50 but only on a small canary set. nothing cluster-wide until later. runtime logs show a lot of grpc "RST_STREAM" and "OUT_OF_ORDER" counters increasing. sample tail from streaming runtime: 
```
2026-03-17T08:13:22Z WARN streaming: token send delayed: deadline_exceeded retries=1 stream_id=0x7f3a
2026-03-17T08:13:24Z ERROR transport: got out-of-order segment seq=348129 ack=348220 ifindex=5
```

liam (sre): pulled a pcap from a host in the affected pool — plenty of reordering. tcpdump snippet (seq/ack simplified):
```
08:12:59.123 IP host-a > host-b: seq 1000 ack 500 win 64240 (out-of-order)
08:12:59.124 IP host-a > host-b: seq 500 ack 500 win 64240
```
looks like buffer scheduling in the leaf switch is delivering segments out-of-order after load-balancing/reshard. also see NIC offload counter spikes (ethtool -S) for GRO/TCP-deferred.

nina (infra): I just checked the SFL leafs — there was an automated firmware push to Broadleaf v2.1.3 at 03:10 that hit ~30% of leafs. vendor notes mention "adaptive queueing" changes.

liam (sre): that aligns. vendor has a known regression where TSO/GRO interacts badly with adaptive queueing, producing packet reordering on multi-queue NICs. quick mitigation options:
- disable GRO/TSO on affected hosts: `ethtool -K ens4 gro off tso off`
- set net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency=1 (reduces coalescing)
- route streaming flows via north-south path (bypass the problematic leaf) until fw fix/rollback
- raise grpc stream deadline temporarily from 200ms -> 450ms and enable fallback smaller batch size

raj (runtime): I can flip deadline + fallback in a hotfix for the streaming router and patch the canary in 15m. will also add logs to surface out-of-order counters per host.

anya (oncall): running `ethtool -K` on three sample hosts now. applying `gro off` to host-a & host-b...

anya (oncall): quick check after `gro off` on host-a/b: reorders metric dropped ~78% and streaming_p95 came down to ~380ms. not fully back to baseline but much better. :thumbsup:

nina (infra): opened ticket with vendor and scheduled a rollback of v2.1.3 on remaining leafs in the pool. k8s-deploy-bot will coordinate with infra to deviate traffic while we roll.

k8s-deploy-bot: rollback plan created: ROLLBACK-1790456789 — targeting 4 leafs at a time, safe-window 30m, smoke after each batch.

liam (sre): for tracking — we should capture: pcap, ethtool -S before/after, rdma link stats (`rdma link show`), and kernel offload counters. RDMA telemetry from one host shows MTU mismatch on the RDMA path (one hop 4092 vs 2048) which can also cause segmentation + reassembly quirks. include that in the vendor ticket.

anya (oncall): good plan. runtime hotfix rolling now (deadline bump + fallback). infra will start rollback in 10m. I'll keep this thread updated with short status checks.

raj (runtime): hotfix canary passed on 3 nodes — increased deadline + fallback reduced client visible retries by ~60%. prepping rollout to rest of pool. :rocket:

nina (infra): rollback batch 1 started. will pause if we see >10% regression in streaming_p95.

anya (oncall): current status at 08:45 UTC — rollback batch1 complete, streaming_p95 baseline restored to ~220-270ms, rpc_retries back to normal. opening incident follow-up doc and tagging eng-runtime + infra for postmortem. :memo:
